children.title: What it is
children.body:
Bureau is a personal to-do, note, idea and writing app for one person. **Everything sits on a grid**: drawers are containers on that grid and open onto grids of their own; objects are everything else, and what an object can do is defined by its attributes.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Version** | 2.98 |
| **Where** | iPhone, installed Safari PWA first |
| **Stack** | Hand-written HTML, CSS, ES modules. No build, no dependencies |
| **Storage** | Local only. Export and import JSON is the bridge |

children.title: The organizing idea
children.body: >> The desk *is* the app. There is no toolbar and no sidebar, only the grid.

children.title: Comparables
children.body:
**Things 3 —** for how a task feels
**Bear —** for how writing feels
**Obsidian —** for what to avoid: infinite nesting and file soup

children.title: Not a product
children.body: Bureau is not for other people. Every design decision is made for **one user**. It is used, for now, to fiddle with rather than live in, and the gap is a layout that fits an actual life.

children.title: The axis now: functions
children.body: What a paper desk lets you *do*: file, annotate, cross-reference, clip, stamp, copy, tear out, pin, date, archive. Fifteen of them are scoped in `docs/FUNCTIONS.md`. Look work is no longer the default answer to "what now".

children.title: Desk
children.body: The home board. Free: as big as what is on it, plus eight empty cells each side.

children.title: Board
children.body: What a container opens onto. A grid of square cells, eight across on a phone.

children.title: Tile
children.body: A stretch of a board, 8 × 14 in a container by default. More are laid by holding the wood beside it.

children.title: Drawer
children.body: A container. In the code, anything carrying the `container` attribute.

children.title: Bench
children.body: A container set up so one activity is easier in it than anywhere else. Once called a flow; `plan` in the code.

children.title: Face
children.body: How a container shows its contents on the outside: a front, a checklist, a calendar, a spine.

children.title: Shape
children.body: A thing's outline: card, note, page, plaque, postcard and the rest.

children.title: Drawer front
children.body: The rail across the bottom on a phone: glass, letter block, knob, padlock. Six places hold any object.

children.title: Top lip
children.body: The board's name, big and on the left, with the gear at its right.

children.title: Carcass
children.body: The wood around the boards.

children.title: Notepad
children.body: A ruled line. Write and press return: it becomes what it reads as.

children.title: Inbox
children.body: A container that makes whatever it reads as. Copper pipes tied to it carry each kind away.

children.title: Rubber stamp
children.body: Press it, then press things: each carries an impression and today's date.

children.title: Spool
children.body: Press it, then two things, and they are tied with string.

children.title: Spiral coin
children.body: Toss it and it makes one of anything, somewhere on the board.

children.title: Garbage bin
children.body: Where a delete goes. Hold one to put it back.

children.title: The fifteen
children.body:
Timothy's master categories, which lead the picker:

Drawer · List · Calendar · Tag · Text · Collage · Jar · Card · Paper · Picture · Video · Audio · Decoration · Doodad · Portal

children.title: Ready benches
children.body:
Brain Dump · Prioritizer · Short Film · Feature Film · Brainstorm · Story Builder · Journal

Every other stock bench is shelved, not deleted. Add a key to `BENCH_READY` to bring one back.

children.title: Five rules
children.body:
1. **Rendering is full re-render.** `render()` rebuilds `#app` from `S`.
2. **An animation never holds anything up.**
3. **Events are delegated**, through `data-act` and one listener set.
4. **Everything is an object; containing is an attribute.**
5. **Never branch on a type's name.** Ask `has(o,'check')`.

children.title: The modules
children.body:
| Module | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| model.js | ATTRS, KINDS, the heart |
| grid.js | Cells, boxes, free spots |
| tiles.js | How a thing looks |
| views.js | The desk and a drawer |
| gestures.js | Drag, hold, swipe |
| motion.js | Every movement |
| persist.js | Storage, migrations, paste |
| wire.js | The one listener |

children.title: Shipping a change
children.body:
- Check it in WebKit first: `node test/safari.mjs`
- The smoke suite is the gate
- Bump `CACHE` and `APP_VERSION` together
- A new file goes in `SHELL`
- Pushing to main deploys to Pages

children.title: Invariants that bite
children.body:
- Layouts are stored **per device**
- Cells are square and measured, never assumed
- Never round the cell size
- `byId(ROOT)` is undefined: ask `container()`
- Image bytes live in IndexedDB, never in the JSON
- Anything that changes a field pushes an undo

children.title: Edges closed or open?
children.body: On a bench's board, closed by default and open on a drawer you made? Or always open unless a bench says so? (NAVIGATION §9)

children.title: Name the tiles?
children.body: Stations: worth naming tiles? The biggest new idea in the navigation scope, and the one Film and Story Builder most want.

children.title: Story Builder as five stations?
children.body: An act per tile, or keep the journey on one tile and make it bigger?

children.title: Which tools to make?
children.body: The compass, the loupe, the ribbon, the pencil ledge: which, if any?

children.title: Merge and push without asking
children.body: The standing instruction: once tested, finished work goes to main.

children.title: Intent recorded
children.body: Functions are the axis. The margin ships first.

children.title: Things that sit on a desk
children.body: Jar, nameplate, string, metronome, hourglass, candle, bell, clock, die.

children.title: The camera tabled
children.body: A note scales up into its surface instead.

children.title: Scope artifact
children.body: Knobs for each aspect of life, verbs for each bench.

children.title: Safari first, American English
children.body: The phone is the primary test.

children.title: The grammar
children.body: How Claude builds boards reliably.

children.title: Navigation scoped
children.body: Gear on the top lip; the bench skill. v2.98.

children.title: What it is
children.body:
A top-down puzzle game where sound is the tool. Coda carries the Composer's Key and fires sound waves through horns, strings, drums and flutes to play the phrase each lock wants.

This repo is the **browser prototype**: a fast-iteration harness for mechanics, which port back into the **Unity** project. No build, no engine. Open a page, paint a room, hear it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **World** | 18 rooms in six areas, 13 × 13 each |
| **Look** | Black and white, sketchy white line-work |
| **Tiles** | 51 × 51 px |

children.title: The Discord
children.body:
**E phrygian · tense · 108 bpm**

The Discord, The Coda, The Unresolved Chord

children.title: The Bell Tower
children.body:
**G mixolydian · confident · 100 bpm**

The Triad, The Stand, The Stair

children.title: The Cloister
children.body:
**D dorian · reflective · 100 bpm**

The Valve, Left and Right, The Slide

children.title: The Undercroft
children.body:
**A aeolian · sad · 88 bpm**

The Kit, The Quiet Room, The Keyboard Floor

children.title: The Reed Gallery
children.body:
**F lydian · mysterious · 96 bpm**

The Flute, The Reed Loft

children.title: The Atrium
children.body:
**C ionian · content · 104 bpm**

Metronome, First Breath, Crossroads, Crossing

children.title: The Unresolved Chord
children.body: The boss: echo its call, resolve its swarm, answer with a chord.

children.title: The Coda
children.body: The last lock listens to the whole world for la-sol-mi-do.

children.title: The Discord
children.body: Dissonants walk on the beat. A wave resolves them. The score gate wants nine.

children.title: The Stair
children.body: The lock wants A; the room is in G. Each step up raises the key.

children.title: The Stand
children.body: Carry the reed from the Reed Loft and set it on the stand.

children.title: The Triad
children.body: Three horns, three forks. Needs three waves in the air at once. The Burin is here.

children.title: The Slide
children.body: Every pull of the slide plays the horn's new note.

children.title: Left and Right
children.body: Find where to stand so the wave meets each head.

children.title: The Valve
children.body: One horn, two forks. Turn the valve, blow again.

children.title: The Keyboard Floor
children.body: Step on K to swing the mallet; press B on the lock to hear its phrase.

children.title: The Quiet Room
children.body: Three string runs, three lengths, three pitches.

children.title: The Kit
children.body: Drums are mirrors, and only the head reflects.

children.title: The Reed Loft
children.body: A reed keeps breathing: a wave every beat for a few beats.

children.title: The Flute
children.body: The note leaves by the first open hole. Cover holes to choose it.

children.title: Crossing
children.body: One wave, two locks, and a circuit that has to get past itself.

children.title: Crossroads
children.body: The tee divides the wave: half out of the bell below, half onward.

children.title: First Breath
children.body: Face right and press A. The wave travels one tile per sixteenth note.

children.title: The Metronome
children.body: Silence until you press B on it; then the tune starts on the next beat.

children.title: How the rooms join
children.body:
Rooms sit on a grid, north to south. Solve a room and its door opens.

**North —** Reed Loft, Flute
**The Atrium row —** Metronome, Brass 01, Brass 02, Brass 03, Triad
**Below it —** Keys 01, Strings 01, Percussion 01, Stand
**The Cloister row —** Brass 04, Percussion 02, Brass 05, Stair
**The Discord —** Unresolved Chord, Coda, Hall

A shortcut from the Reed Loft back to Brass 01 opens only from the far side.

children.title: Horn
children.body: Mouthpiece in, bells out. Tees divide a wave; valves turn; every tubing structure is a horn.

children.title: Slide
children.body: An instrument on its own: every pull plays the horn's new note.

children.title: Strings
children.body: Three runs, three lengths, three pitches. Pegs face their string.

children.title: Piano keys
children.body: Stepped on, they swing a mallet. They autotile, sixteen cases.

children.title: Drums
children.body: Mirrors in 45° steps. Only the head reflects; the back swallows the wave.

children.title: Flute
children.body: The fingering picks the note and the way out: the first open hole.

children.title: Reed
children.body: Keeps breathing: a wave a beat for several beats.

children.title: Hi-hat
children.body: Ticks. No puzzle yet.

children.title: Strumentino
children.body: A blank per-face instrument. No puzzle yet.

children.title: The Burin
children.body: Lifts drums and reeds into the satchel (L) and turns the one in hand (R).

children.title: Overtones
children.body: An upgrade: more waves in the air at once.

children.title: Dissonant
children.body: A sour note that walks on the beat and shoves Coda. Any wave resolves it.

children.title: Everything in time
children.body: The wave travels **one tile per sixteenth note** at the room's bpm, and every sound is synchronized to it. `test/timing.mjs` checks it. Waves carry on through open doors, and a lock can listen to the whole world.

children.title: Keys, modes, motif
children.body: Each area is one key, mode and tempo, with a title card. Stairs climb: up raises the key. A four-bar motif gains a layer per solved room, ten in all, played in each area's mode.

children.title: Should dissonance matter?
children.body: A sour wave still lights every lock. Should note locks reject soured notes, or a sour wave fail to light a fork?

children.title: Is the boss fun on a phone?
children.body: Phase three wants the longest horn first and a beat to land all three. Fun or fiddly?

children.title: Does the tune work?
children.body: The motif was composed blind. Nobody has listened to it yet: judge it by ear.

children.title: Hi-hat and strumentino?
children.body: Both are in the game with no puzzle of their own. What should each one do?

children.title: The Y axis trap
children.body:
The prototype is **+y down**. Unity 2D is **+y up**, so every rotation flips.

| | here | Unity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CW | (-y, x) | (y, -x) |
| up | (0, -1) | (0, 1) |

Copy the intent (`Redirect90CW`), not the arithmetic.

children.title: Art protocol
children.body:
Black and white. A **3 px** main line. Ornament grows from the form. 51 × 51 tiles. Joined pieces change texture to show it.

Real art exists for **15** slots; **41** are still placeholders.

children.title: Room report
children.body: Says what a room does: its pitch range, the piece that carries it, the piece nothing reaches.

children.title: Art parity
children.body: Black and white line-work; square rooms; doors lead to rooms.

children.title: The play screen
children.body: Zelda-style bars, movable controls, Coda moves like Link.

children.title: The dungeon pass
children.body: Sixteen interconnected rooms, woodwinds, the Burin, a motif that grows.

children.title: After playing it
children.body: The boss, the metronome room, typing that sings, floors tinted by mode.

children.title: What it is
children.body:
An interactive map of **every publicly accessible outdoor place** in Connecticut and New York, built to be released.

Everything is precomputed. The site fetches no live data and does no classification in the browser: a visit costs about **290 KB and a third of a second**.

>> Find a park near me, verified that it's a good park, go there and get all the info.

children.title: Can I go there?
children.body: Green fill is public land. The popup says whether by right or by the owner's permission.

children.title: Who runs it?
children.body: Border color: state green, federal brown, town blue, land trust teal, cemetery purple.

children.title: What kind of place?
children.body: The pin's icon, plus chips for trails, water, sports, playground, historic and parking.

children.title: How do I get there?
children.body: Every road both states record, drawn at every zoom: 617,634 of them, with footpaths.

children.title: The data files
children.body:
| File | Size | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| places.json | ~2 MB | Every place, classified |
| everypark.pmtiles | 13.6 MB | Boundaries and trails, zooms 6–14 |
| roads.pmtiles | 65 MB | 617,634 roads, none dropped at any zoom |

children.title: Publishing: one rule
children.body:
!!! Data flows only through the Actions.

Edit `data/verified.json` or code, commit, push. `publish.yml` applies it and deploys in about ninety seconds. A local deploy must never touch `data/`.

children.title: How sure is it?
children.body: CT is **72%** verified, NY **60%**, and the two do not rest on the same kind of evidence. The app shows a binary today where the data supports a gradient: `researched`, `sources`, `checked`.

children.title: The 3D view
children.body: An isometric island per park, elevation mapped onto the polygon, season and time of day changing the palette. **The centerpiece**, not a novelty beside the map.

children.title: Show how sure the data is
Depth on land that can be verified
The rest of the card icons
A gradient, but how?
children.body: Which signals make a place "sure": a cited source, a site visit, an official list? And how should a pin show it?

children.title: Easements: hide or dim?
children.body: Shaky-provenance spots are deprioritized, not deleted. Should they look different on the map?

children.title: Not next
children.body: **More states.** New York and Connecticut only for now; New England eventually. Each state costs a rules audit, not just a fetch.
